pages.quiz:
ENGLISH — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. goed
   C. going
   D. went

2. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1 Extensive Listening.

3. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. No full stops
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

4. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

5. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. Only a joining word
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only an action

6. When practising Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.

7. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.

9. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.

10. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.

11. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. quickly
   C. happiness
   D. blue

12. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.

13. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. where is the library

14. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.

15. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 5.2.1 Intensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in use 5.3 .1 Word Classes: Adverbs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Phrases and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 5.4.1 Functional Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Responsive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 6.1.2 Speaking Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 6.2.1 Reading Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Word Classes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Clauses: and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
